metadata.title: The nature of hypervelocity stars as inferred from their galactic trajectories

black hole.

notes: Table 1 explicitly groups four stars under “Unbound:” and the final text states that 8 of the 12 stars are bound, so SDSS J110224.37+025002.8, SDSS J115245.91-021116.2, SDSS J144955.58+310351.4, and SDSS J113312.12+010824.9 (HVS 7) are treated as retained unbound candidates. The eight Table 1 stars under “Bound:” are included as follow_up because they belong to the previously surveyed HVS sample, although this paper concludes that they are bound. For SDSS J110224.37+025002.8 and SDSS J115245.91-021116.2, the BHB rows list v=461 versus v_esc=493 and v=494 versus v_esc=511, respectively, despite being placed under “Unbound:”; the paper’s final preference for massive main-sequence stars supports retaining their MS-based unbound classification, but this apparent inconsistency is noted. SDSS J172226.55+594155.9 is excluded: the paper ultimately identifies it as a halo object rather than an HVS and does not retain it as an unbound candidate.

SDSS J074950.24+243841.2: Table 1 (T:p4-b0; I:p4-b0) reports cylindrical Galactocentric radius R and height z, not the required three-dimensional galactocentric radius, so R is not extracted as galactocentric_radius and no conversion is made. The target is listed under “Bound,” but no numerical bound or unbound probability is reported. No target-specific equatorial coordinates, heliocentric distance, parallax, or radial velocity are explicitly tabulated; the table's v is the total present-day speed in the Galactic rest frame.

SDSS J075055.24+472822.9: Table 1 (T:p4-b0 and I:p4-b0) reports for SDSS J075055.24+472822.9 the cylindrical Galactic radius R and height z, not a three-dimensional galactocentric radius, so no galactocentric_radius is extracted under the stated definition. The paper does not report a heliocentric distance, parallax, or target-specific radial velocity. The target's RA/Dec appear only encoded in its identifier and are not treated as separately reported astrometry. Table 1 defines v as the present-day speed in the rest frame of the Galaxy; the text at T:p2-b20 describes it as the lab-frame speed. No bound or unbound probability is reported for this star; it is only placed in the Bound section of Table 1.

SDSS J075712.93+512938.0: The paper's Table 1 (T:p4-b0 / I:p4-b0) lists for SDSS J075712.93+512938.0 only the proper motions, cylindrical galactocentric radius R (29.3 kpc MS, 12.7 kpc BHB), height above the plane z (12.8 kpc MS, 2.8 kpc BHB), present-day Galactic-rest-frame speed v, escape speed, ejection speed, and time since ejection. R is a cylindrical radius and z a vertical height, so neither is entered as galactocentric_radius (3D distance to the Galactic centre); no parallax, distance, RA/Dec or radial velocity is reported individually for this star. The star is listed under the "Bound:" heading of Table 1, but no bound/unbound probability is quantified, so no bound_probability value is recorded. Values retained from both the MS and BHB trajectory cases, as the paper reports both without preferring one.

SDSS J081828.07+570922.1: Table 1 reports R [kpc] and z [kpc] separately, not a three-dimensional galactocentric radius; they were not combined or converted. The target is listed under “Bound,” but the paper does not report a bound probability. No heliocentric distance, parallax, or current radial velocity for this target is explicitly given in the supplied table/text.

SDSS J090710.08+365957.5: Table 1's R and z values are cylindrical Galactic radius and vertical height, not the three-dimensional galactocentric radius required here, so no galactocentric_radius was extracted. The tabulated proper motions are model proper motions chosen to be consistent with a Galactic Centre origin, not independently measured proper motions; separate MS and BHB cases are retained. No RA, Dec, distance, parallax, or individual radial velocity is reported for this star in the supplied material.

SDSS J140432.38+352258.4: Table 1 lists R (cylindrical Galactic radius) and z (height above the plane), not the three-dimensional galactocentric radius, so no galactocentric_radius value was extracted. The table gives no per-star bound probability or radial velocity for SDSS J140432.38+352258.4.

SDSS J141723.34+101245.7: Table 1 at T:p4-b0 places SDSS J141723.34+101245.7 in the Bound sample and gives separate MS and BHB rows. The tabulated R and z are cylindrical Galactic radius and height, not a three-dimensional galactocentric radius, so no galactocentric_radius value was extracted. The text at T:p2-b21/T:p3-b3 says this star becomes unbound if the halo mass is halved, but reports no bound/unbound probability. No individual RA, Dec, distance, parallax, or radial velocity is reported for this star in the supplied material.

SDSS J142001.94+124404.8: Table 1 (T:p4-b0) gives separate MS and BHB results for SDSS J142001.94+124404.8. It reports cylindrical Galactocentric R and height z, not a three-dimensional galactocentric radius, and I did not calculate one from R and z. It also does not report the target's RA, Dec, heliocentric distance, parallax, or heliocentric radial velocity. The tabulated v is the present-day speed in the Galactic rest frame, not a line-of-sight radial velocity. The star is listed under "Bound," but no numerical bound or unbound probability is reported.

SDSS J110224.37+025002.8: The target is listed in Table 1 under "Unbound"; the paper reports no bound/unbound probability for it. Table 1 gives cylindrical Galactocentric coordinates R and z, not the three-dimensional distance to the Galactic centre, so no galactocentric_radius is recorded. The paper does not report an individual radial velocity, parallax, or distance for this star in the supplied material.

SDSS J115245.91-021116.2: Table 1 (T:p4-b0, I:p4-b0) lists the target under "Unbound" and reports R and z separately; R is explicitly cylindrical Galactic radius, so no three-dimensional galactocentric radius is recorded. The paper does not report individual right ascension, declination, distance, parallax, or heliocentric radial velocity for this star, and it gives no numerical bound/unbound probability for it; the table's bound/unbound grouping is a classification rather than a probability. The tabulated proper motions are the values most consistent with a Galactic Centre origin under each assumed evolutionary stage.

SDSS J144955.58+310351.4: The target is listed under "Unbound" in Table 1 (T:p4-b0), but the paper does not report a numerical bound or unbound probability for it, so no probability was extracted. Table 1 gives R and z, but these are cylindrical Galactocentric coordinates, not the three-dimensional Galactocentric radius; no conversion was performed. No heliocentric distance, parallax, or heliocentric radial velocity is explicitly reported for this star, and the equatorial coordinates encoded in the identifier were not converted into numerical ra/dec.

SDSS J113312.12+010824.9: Table 1 gives R and z separately as cylindrical Galactic radius and height, not a three-dimensional Galactocentric distance, so no galactocentric_radius value is extracted. The text's v_rf = 418 km/s for HVS 7 (T:p1-b12) is a Galactic-rest-frame line-of-sight component, so it is not treated as a heliocentric radial velocity or as the total Galactic-rest-frame speed; the total speed is taken from Table 1 (T:p4-b0).
